description: S459 copy-in, the positive semantics (every write here is legitimate): (1) after `@rows.push(r)`, editing `r` (`r.n = 9`) does not reach the stored row — @rows[1].n stays 2. (2) `@other = @rows` stores @other's own copy: `@other[0].n = 7` changes @other only; @rows[0].n stays 1. (3) whole writes built from the cell's own value (`@ls = [...@ls, 3]`) and later element writes keep working.
rationale: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S459 "a, go" — a refined cell stores its own copy of everything it admits (the pushed element on push, the whole value on assignment); analogy:§66.10 (aliases snapshot). The direction of change for refined cells: after `@rows.push(@draft)`, editing `@draft` no longer changes the row.
